name: How does surface preparation for painting differ in a whole-home remodel compared to minor repairs?

mainEntity.name: How does surface preparation for painting differ in a whole-home remodel compared to minor repairs?

acceptedAnswer.text: In a whole-home remodel, surface preparation for painting is significantly more comprehensive than for minor repairs. It often involves extensive drywall replacement or repair due to structural changes, plumbing or electrical work, and the removal of old fixtures. This necessitates a full range of tasks, including mudding, taping, sanding, and priming large areas to create perfectly smooth canvases. For AKN Design Group, this meticulous preparation is foundational to achieving the high-quality finish expected in a substantial renovation. In contrast, minor repairs might only involve light sanding and spot priming, which falls outside our specialization in comprehensive projects.
acceptedAnswer.description: Surface preparation in a whole-home remodel involves extensive drywall repair, mudding, sanding, and priming due to structural changes. This is far more comprehensive than the light sanding and spot priming typical for minor repairs.
